question: Identify the INCORRECT pair of cropping season and related crop from the following.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rabi - Paddy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Paddy (rice)** is predominantly a **Kharif crop**, grown during the monsoon season due to its high water requirement.
 
• Kharif crops are typically sown at the onset of the monsoon (June-July) and harvested in the autumn (September-October).
 
• Rabi crops, such as wheat and mustard, are grown in the winter season and harvested in the spring (March-April).
 
• Examples of Kharif crops include paddy, maize, soyabean, and cotton, whereas Rabi crops include wheat, barley, peas, and gram.
 
• The pairing of "Rabi - Paddy" is incorrect as paddy is not suited for the low rainfall and cooler conditions of the Rabi season.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rabi Crops:**

 
 
• These crops are sown in winter (October-November) and harvested in spring (March-April).
 
• They require cool weather for growth and less water compared to Kharif crops.
 
• Examples: Wheat, barley, mustard, peas, and gram.
 
 
 
• **Kharif Crops:**
 
 
• Sown with the onset of the monsoon (June-July) and harvested in autumn (September-October).
 
• They require hot and humid weather with substantial rainfall.
 
• Examples: Paddy, maize, soyabean, cotton, and sugarcane.
 
 
 
• **Classification of Crops:**
 
 
• Crops in India are broadly classified into three types based on the season: Kharif, Rabi, and Zaid.
 
• Zaid crops are grown between Rabi and Kharif seasons (March to June), e.g., watermelon, cucumber, and fodder crops.
 
 
 
• **Water Requirements for Paddy:**
 
 
• Paddy is a water-intensive crop that requires standing water for growth.
 
• It thrives in areas with heavy rainfall or where irrigation facilities are available.
